questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a functional dependency?

options.text: A relationship where one attribute uniquely determines another.
A relationship where an attribute is dependent on multiple tables.
A constraint that ensures data integrity across databases.
A rule that specifies the data type of an attribute.

questions.explanation: A functional dependency exists when one attribute uniquely determines another. This is crucial for database normalization, ensuring that each piece of information is stored in exactly one place.

questions.stem: In a database with attributes A, B, and C, which of the following is a functional dependency?
questions.explanation: The functional dependency A, B \rightarrow C indicates that the combination of A and B uniquely determines C. This is a typical example of a functional dependency in a relational database.

questions.stem: Given a relation R(A, B, C) with functional dependencies A \rightarrow B and B \rightarrow C, what is the size of the closure of {A}? Provide your answer as a number.
questions.explanation: The closure of {A} is {A, B, C} because A \rightarrow B and B \rightarrow C imply A \rightarrow C. Thus, the size of the closure is 3.

questions.stem: What type of anomaly occurs when deleting a record results in the loss of other valuable data?
questions.explanation: A deletion anomaly occurs when deleting a record leads to the unintended loss of additional data. This can happen if the database is not properly normalized.

questions.explanation: Functional dependencies can lead to update anomalies when a change in one attribute necessitates changes in multiple records. For instance, if a student's address is stored in multiple records, updating the address in one record but not others can lead to inconsistency.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of functional dependencies implies A \rightarrow C?
questions.explanation: The set {A \rightarrow B, B \rightarrow C} implies A \rightarrow C through transitivity. If A determines B and B determines C, then A also determines C.

questions.stem: Describe an insertion anomaly and provide an example in the context of a database with attributes: EmployeeID, Department, and Project.
markingGuide: Describes how it occurs in the given context.

questions.explanation: An insertion anomaly occurs when certain attributes cannot be inserted into the database without the presence of other attributes.
